page0.text:
It's after 10:00 PM now.
"It's time. We should go, Shirou."
Tohsaka appears, ready to leave.
"I know. Take care of the house, Sakura."

page1.text:
Tohsaka and I will go out on patrol, as planned.
...It sounds stupid to think that we can fight back against Zouken by patrolling the town, but that's all we can do at the moment.

page2.text:
The enemies we have to beat are Zouken, Assassin, Saber, and that mysterious Shadow.
To be honest, there's no way we can beat them in a straight fight.
I just have to be patient while Tohsaka comes up with countermeasures.

page3.text:
Despite that, we can't stay cooped up in the house.
As the news said this morning, Zouken has started attacking civilians.
We might not be able to beat him now, but I don't think it's a waste to try and prevent more people from falling victim.

page4.text:
"..."
"..."
I put on my shoes without saying anything.
Both of us know how dangerous it is to go out at night.
Even if Zouken is only after Sakura, he might consider it a nuisance if we're walking around town.
...In the worst case, what happened in the forest might happen again.
The thought doesn't make me very talkative.

page5.text:
"...Hey. What's your problem?"
And then...
I'm not in the mood even for a serious talk, but I look up to see Tohsaka staring at me.

page6.text:
"If you're just seeing us off, that's fine. Behave and go back to your room, Sakura."
"..."
Staring through me, to be exact.
She's glaring at Sakura, who's standing in the hallway.

page7.text:
"Nee-san. I think I should go with you after all. It's too dangerous out there for the two of you alone."
"Sakura..."
So that's why she's here.
I appreciate the sentiment, but we have to stick to the plan.

page8.text: "No. You know that Zouken is after you. You need to stay here with Illya and protect yourselves."

page9.text:
"I know that. But you can't move one of your arms, and Nee-san doesn't have a Servant anymore, so..."
"Cut the crap, Sakura. You're still our enemy. I can't trust someone that might turn into Zouken's puppet at any second to watch my back."

page10.text:
"Ah... But, Nee-san..."
"You just need to protect yourself. If you feel bad for us at all, then don't create more work for us by pulling something like this. You just need to have Rider protect yourself and Illya."

page11.text:
"Tohsaka, you don't have to—hey!"
"Come on, get your head in the game. There might be new victims while we stand around talking."
Tohsaka grabs my hand and pulls me out of the house.

page12.text: "Ah... A-anyway, be careful, Sakura! Take care of Illya!"

page14.text:
"Hey, Tohsaka! Hold on! I'm coming with you, so let go of my hand."
"Hmph. It's your fault for taking your sweet time."
Tohsaka releases my hand and stops power walking.

page15.text:
"What? If you have something to say, say it."
She's being like this now,
all rushed and weirdly belligerent.
Good grief.
If you're that self-conscious about it, then you didn't need to use that tone with her, idiot.

page16.text: "...Haah. Fine, I'll say it. Don't be so hard on Sakura. She didn't ask to be in this situation."

page17.text: "I know that. But I had to be firm with her. If she doesn't commit to this, it'll make her easier for Zouken to exploit."

page18.text:
"...I'm not sympathizing with Sakura.
I had nothing to do with her being Zouken's puppet or being adopted by the Matous. That's her own problem, and I can't fix any of that just by talking about it."

page19.text:
"Tohsaka..."
"I'm only at that house because of you, not Sakura. Got that?
My goal is to get the Holy Grail, not save her.
To do that, I need to keep an eye on Sakura, even if she hates me for it. That's why I talked to her that way, and I'm going to keep treating her as my enemy."

page20.text:
"...So you don't care if she hates you? Because you're total strangers?"
"That's right. You got a problem with that?"
"Of course I do, stupid."

page21.text:
...That's so like Tohsaka.
She's normally so bold and decisive, but right now, I can see her clenching her fist and trying her best to convince herself.

page22.text:
"All right. If that's how you want to play this, then go ahead.
No matter how you decide to act, Sakura knows how you really feel."

page23.text:
"Wha...what do you mean, how I really feel!?"
"How much you care about her, I mean. If even an outsider like me can notice it, then Sakura sees right through you."

page24.text:
"Ngh... You don't understand. I just, um..."
"I do understand. People don't feel sincere anger for someone they don't care about. That's why you're stern with her, right? You don't say it out loud, but you think of her as your precious little sister."
"Y-you don't know what you're talking about! Stop pushing my buttons like that, you dummy!!!!"

page25.text:
Tohsaka is so angry she becomes red in the face.
But it doesn't have its usual impact, which tells me enough.

page27.text: "Okay. Then let me bug you with this. I want you and Sakura to get along. Sakura likes you, and you like her too, so I don't like seeing the two of you act the way you did earlier."

page28.text:
"...You know, I did say that she's my enemy. That won't change just because I'm nice to her. To begin with...how are we supposed to be friends, after all this time?"
"Just keep doing what you've been doing. Have some faith in yourself, Tohsaka. I think you're being a good big sister."

page29.text:
"Ngh... W-we're wasting time! Let's go to the crime scene we saw on the news!"
Tohsaka spins on her heel and stomps off.
I follow her with an absentminded "sure, sure."
But then...

page30.text:
"Shirou."
She says my name without looking at me,
"Um, thanks. That made me happy."
and grumbles, embarrassed.

page31.text:
...There's no one at the central park.
It isn't particularly crowded even during the day, and now it's extra quiet after last night's murders.
The park wasn't built as a place to rest between the office buildings. It's no different from an undeveloped wasteland.

page32.text: "Murders, huh? They aren't treating it as an accident. Well, it's hard to tell because they don't know exactly who died or where the bodies are, but it's suspicious that they're calling them murders."

page33.text:
There are still bloodstains on the grass.
Quite a lot of blood, spilled in four separate areas.
They're some distance from the blackened ground, probably because the victims tried to run away.

page34.text: "Tohsaka. You said that Zouken didn't do this, but what do you think now? Has your impression changed now that we're here?"

page35.text:
"...Let me think. I thought the Shadow did this, but now I'm not so sure.
Whenever it shows up, it sucks in all the mana around it. But this place isn't dry of mana... I still think that whatever happened here was an unplanned meal, though."

page36.text:
That's all we manage to learn from the scene.
We leave the site of the tragedy.

page37.text:
...We don't find anything else of note in Shinto.
Given how conspicuous last night's incident was, it's possible that Zouken's group is trying to keep a low profile tonight.

page38.text:
It's almost midnight.
Tohsaka and I head home, feeling a cool breeze from the riverbank.
I ask her a question on the way.
"Tohsaka. Sakura's the successor to the Matous, right?"
I've been curious about something for a while.

page39.text:
"Why are you asking now? It's not a secret anymore."
"No, I mean, if she's their successor, that means she's a mage. I was wondering what kind of magecraft she uses."
"Oh, that."

page40.text: "...Well, I've heard that the Matous use magecraft related to binding and compulsion. The Command Spells wouldn't exist without them."

page41.text:
"Huh. So does Sakura's magecraft have something do with restraints? But that would mean..."
That day.
The magecraft that Sakura unleashed when the Crest Worms were attacking her must have been Rider's power.

page42.text:
"I...don't think so. That was a Makiri spell, but not the kind of magecraft they specialize in.
There's no point in thinking about it, anyway. Sakura doesn't have the magical energy to power magecraft. The Crest Worms eat her extra energy, so she shouldn't be able to cast any magecraft."

page43.text:
"...Okay, good. But how strong is she, from your perspective? Are you on the same level, since you're both family heirs?"
"She has about the same number of Magic Circuits as me.
Did you forget that we're actual sisters?"

page44.text:
"Oh."
Right, now that she mentions it.
That's why the Matous adopted her, to begin with.

page45.text:
"So she's as strong as you are?"
"I'm not sure. I can use the Five Great Elements, while she was apparently born with an affinity for Imaginary Elements. But she's Water-aligned now, so they must have forced that onto her. What do you think would happen if you forced a bird that flies in the air to swim in the ocean?"

page46.text:
"It would die, or..."
"Yeah. It would take everything just to adapt to being underwater.
She would have been successful as a Tohsaka, but after what the Matous did to her, she's no different from you.
No, you're actually a lot stronger than her because you're physically trained."

page47.text:
"So, hypothetically, if you two got into a magical duel..."
"I would win ten times out of ten. Sakura doesn't have the magical energy capacity to pierce my defenses."

page48.text:
...I see.
I don't know what kind of magecraft Sakura can use, but her power dynamic with Tohsaka is clear.
Tohsaka isn't the type to brag, so she's probably just stating the facts.

page49.text:
"...This is embarrassing. I never even knew Sakura was a mage, and I don't know how skilled she is. I feel pretty stupid calling myself her protector."
"You know, the Crest Worms are constantly feeding on her magical energy. You can't even tell she's a mage up close."

page50.text: "Plus, she's been trying her best to hide it from you. So whatever you do, don't bring this up in front of her."

page51.text:
"..."
Yeah, don't need to tell me twice.
Even if Sakura is a mage, she's still Sakura.
I'm not sophisticated enough to play games with her, anyway.
No matter who she is, all I can do is treat her the same way I always have.

page52.text:
"Yeah. If you think so, then I'll keep treating her the same way.
I just won't ask for her help as a mage. That's okay, right?"

page53.text: "Of course. And if you ever do, I'll take her back to my house instead."

page54.text:
The way she says it so gently with a smile makes my heart skip a beat.
...See?
You're a great big sister, Tohsaka.

page55.text:
"I guess that wouldn't work, though. She only smiles when she's at your place. That was what surprised me the most yesterday."
That was a surprise?
The thought seems to make Tohsaka so happy.

page56.text:
"Huh? What do you mean, she smiled?"
That's how she always is.

page57.text:
"Yeah. I was always worried about that.
You know, I don't talk to her much, so I try to look out for her whenever I can. She's been hanging around the kyudo club ever since we ended up in the same school."

page58.text:
"Yeah, I know that."
"...Mm-hm. And after a while, I noticed something. She never smiles."

page59.text:
...
That...
...sounds pretty believable, even though I'm only hearing it for the first time.
Now that I think about it, Sakura's always pretty gloomy at school.

page60.text:
"But even that's different when you're around.
She would always smile when you came to visit the club.
Meaning that she's only ever happy when Shirou Emiya is with her."
